newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN warns of NKorea catastrophe if food aid delayed.
newsitem.headline: UN warns of NKorea catastrophe if food aid delayed.

text.p: The United Nations food agency said on Friday that North Korea was on the verge of famine and urgently appealed for funds to finance aid to stop starvation.

The World Food Programme (WFP), the main agency involved in getting supplies into North Korea, said it had raised only $34 million out of an appeal for $95 million for North Korea and this was far from enough to meet emergency needs.
"Time is running out. We are on the brink of famine (in North Korea)," WFP spokeswoman Christiane Berthiaume said.
"We need funds as quickly as possible if we want to avoid a catastrophe. We need an urgent response," she told a briefing.

The secretive communist country of 24 million people, badly hit by two harvest failures due to heavy rains and flooding in 1995 and 1996, faces a food shortage of more than 1 million metric tons this year, according to experts.
North Korea told aid agencies earlier this month that 134 children had died from malnutrition in its worsening food crisis. Some aid officials fear the true figure may be higher.

The latest WFP warning followed an appeal this week by North Korean representatives for substantial international assistance at a meeting in New York with South Korean and U.S. diplomats, called to hear Pyongyang's answer to a proposal for peace talks.
Seoul and Washington insist large-scale aid can only be discussed at four-nation peace talks, also including China.
U.S. humanitarian aid agencies have urged the Clinton administration to drop demands for concessions from North Korea and ship massive food aid.
But Washington officials said on Thursday no new U.S. food aid pledges were expected before North Korea responded conclusively to the peace talks.
Berthiaume said WFP hoped to distribute 60,000 tonnes of food in North Korea in May, way below the 203,000 tonnes envisaged under its appeal, launched earlier in April.
She said a first U.S. ship was due to arrive in North Korea on May 4 with 5,000 tonnes of maize and soya mix and 8,500 tonnes of maize on board.
A second U.S. aid shipment of 6,600 tonnes of rice, 1,700 tonnes of maize-soya mix and 6,900 tonnes of maize would follow by May 20.
"All this is not sufficient to respond to a situation which is deteriorating day by day," Berthiaume said.
